name: Pierre Levegh
features: fair skin, dark hair receding, dark eyes, long narrow face, high forehead, prominent nose, lean spare build, grave reserved expression
bio: Born Pierre Bouillin, he raced under the name of his uncle Alfred Velghe, a pioneer killed in 1904. He is remembered for the 1952 Le Mans, which he drove solo for twenty-three hours with a four-lap lead before the crankshaft broke an hour from the flag. In 1955 his Mercedes was launched into the crowd at Le Mans, killing him and more than eighty spectators, and changing motor racing’s attitude to safety for good.
